newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Miners strike at Coal & Allied mine.
newsitem.headline: Miners strike at Coal & Allied mine.

text.p: Workers at Coal and Allied Industries Ltd's Hunter Valley Number One thermal coal mine went on strike at midnight on Wednesday over stalled enterprise bargaining negotiations, Coal and Allied said.
The company, which is 71 percent owned by Rio Tinto Ltd, said the strike at the mine in the state of New South Wales would cost A$1 million a day in lost revenue.
Coal and Allied's general manager of Hunter Valley Number One, Allan Davies, said in a statement the company had accommodated some employee's demands for alternative employment arrangements.
"The unions have told us, however, that they will not continue negotiating the enterprise agreement while alternative employment arrangements are available," Davies said.
The mine's main customers are Japanese and East Asian power utilities and has a capital value of A$430 million.
It usually produces up to 7.5 million tonnes of coal a year and has 550 workers.
